editorial:
Three sisters sneak into a senator’s house to grab bribe money, but the job turns into a nightmare when strange cries lead them to the basement. The setup is simple and tense, and the movie keeps you watching because every room feels like it is hiding something. The sisters are not perfect heroes, which makes their bad choices feel believable, and the house itself becomes a character with dark corners and locked doors. You get a mix of heist tension and horror dread, so even when the scares are quiet, the mood stays uneasy.

The acting is solid, especially when fear takes over and the sisters start turning on each other. The pacing moves well, though some scenes repeat the same basement tension a little too long. The scares are more creepy than gory, so it works best for viewers who like slow dread and mystery. If you want a polished night-in horror pick, stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the sisters discover the chained girl is connected to the house’s dark secret, not just a prisoner. After a violent fight, the last surviving sister makes it out, but the final twist shows the evil has followed her. The movie ends on a chilling note that suggests the nightmare is not over and the danger has only changed shape.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creepy house horror and tense survival stories.
